chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Musa ibn Ja'far, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the man who has a slave girl, and the son of his son falls upon her before the grandfather has had intercourse with her; or the man commits adultery with the woman, so would it be permissible for his father to marry her? He (peace be upon him) said: No. Rather, that is when the man marries her, so he has intercourse with her, then his son commits adultery with her, it would not harm him, because the prohibited does not spoil the permissible, and similarly is the case with the slave girl.
ai.seo_question: Does a son's adultery with a woman invalidate his father's marriage to her?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the son's subsequent adultery does not invalidate the father's prior valid marriage, illustrating the principle that 'the prohibited does not corrupt the permissible' (al-haram la yufsidu al-halal). This ruling is specifically derived from the context of a slave girl, highlighting the distinct legal status of concubinage versus marriage in Shia jurisprudence, where the father's ownership and consummation establish the bond regardless of the son's illicit act.
